title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: TRY NUMBER TWELVE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight: Hollis Pratt, a crawfish fry cook in Shreveport, Louisiana.
A pack a day for thirty-seven years. He has quit eleven times.
This is number twelve.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE WAITING ROOM
segments.quote: Health is not valued till sickness comes.
segments.author: Thomas Fuller
lines: At his checkup, Hollis was out of breath from the parking lot.
A sign in the waiting room quoted the old English writer Thomas Fuller:
Health is not valued till sickness comes.
The doctor said, Hollis, sickness is already in the parking lot.
Hollis sat in his truck a long time. He did not light up.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE WHY
segments.quote: He who has a why to live can bear almost any how.
segments.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
lines: Eleven times he quit because somebody told him to.
His wife Darlene had underlined a line from the German thinker Nietzsche:
He who has a why to live can bear almost any how.
So Hollis wrote his why on a card: Grand Canyon. With Darlene.
He promised her that trip in nineteen ninety-four. They went to Biloxi instead.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: DOWN THE STAIRS
segments.quote: Habit is habit, and not to be flung out of the window by any man, but coaxed down-stairs a step at a time.
segments.author: Mark Twain
lines: Day one, he quit cold. By noon, he was yelling at a crawfish.
His boss, Miss Bea, read him Mark Twain off her phone:
Habit is habit, and not to be flung out of the window by any man, but coaxed down-stairs a step at a time.
So Hollis cut one cigarette a week, and walked the parking lot on every break.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE LEVEE
segments.quote: Those who think they have not time for bodily exercise will sooner or later have to find time for illness.
segments.author: Edward Stanley
lines: Soon he walked the Red River levee every morning. Well, most mornings.
So Darlene taped a note to the coffee maker, from the British statesman Edward Stanley:
Those who think they have not time for bodily exercise will sooner or later have to find time for illness.
The first week, a man with a walker passed him. Twice.
By spring, Hollis passed the man with the walker. They waved.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE BAD FRIDAY
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: On day ninety, the fryer broke on a busy Friday. Hollis smoked one behind the dumpster.
He drove home sure number twelve was dead.
Then he saw his coffee can of cigarette money, with a Ben Franklin line on the lid:
Little strokes fell great oaks.
Almost eight hundred dollars. One bad Friday didn't erase that. Next morning, he walked.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE BIG CANYON
segments.quote: Victory is sweetest when you've known defeat.
segments.author: Malcolm Forbes
lines: One year later, Hollis and Darlene stood at the Grand Canyon. The coffee can paid.
He hiked a mile down and back up, barely out of breath.
He thought of that bad Friday, and of the magazine man Malcolm Forbes:
Victory is sweetest when you've known defeat.
Darlene took his picture. Thirty years late, and right on time.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Listen. Find your why. Go slow. Walk. Get back up.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Listen to the warning. Find your why. Go slow. Walk. Get back up.
Me? I quit dessert once. It lasted until dessert.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
